sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in College Station, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. A College Station owner can sell quickly through a cash buyer, through an agent with a short listing window, or directly to a neighbor or investor, and the right route depends on the condition of the house and how soon the money is needed.

College Station sits in Brazos County and is built around Texas A&M University. That shapes who buys and who rents here, and it shapes the timing of a sale more than in most Texas cities.

  • Cash buyer: one offer, no showings, closing on a date you pick. The price is usually below what a fully repaired home brings on the open market.
  • Agent listing: the widest exposure and often the highest price, but you carry showings, buyer financing delays and repair requests.
  • Sale to an investor with an as-is contract: similar to a cash sale, with the buyer inspecting but you doing no work.
  • Keep and rent: possible, but College Station requires registration of non-owner-occupied houses, covered below.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about housing in College Station?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau describes a city where most households rent and homes are valued well above the local income level. The table below repeats what its QuickFacts page prints for College Station.

With only about a third of homes lived in by their owners, a house for sale here often competes with plentiful rentals. Buyers who plan to rent it out are a natural audience for an as-is sale. The estimate shows 5.8% growth from the April 2020 base.

sections.h2: How did College Station become a college town?
sections.html:
The city grew out of the college itself. The city website says Texas A&M, the first state institution of higher education in Texas, opened in 1876, and the Postal Service designated the area College Station in 1877, taking the name from a railroad station west of campus.

Residents voted 217 to 39 on October 19, 1938 to incorporate, and the city adopted a home rule charter in 1952 once its population passed 5,000. The same city page describes the University as home to nearly 80,000 students and lists a research hub developed with Texas A&M and the City of Bryan as part of the growth plan.

For a seller the practical meaning is a house market tied to the academic calendar, football weekends and a large pool of renters. The city page also notes that the George H.W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum draws more than 125,000 visitors a year, which is one reason short-term rental rules matter on this side of town.

sections.h2: Do I have to register a rental house in College Station?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's rental housing page says every single-family, townhome, duplex, tri-plex, four-plex, five-plex or six-plex dwelling that is not owner occupied must be registered, whether or not rent is charged.

The page lists a one-time fee of $90 per building as of October 24, 2022, and says licenses no longer need annual renewal. Owners who do not live in the city need a local contact living within 30 miles of City Hall. Changes of ownership or contact details go to the rental registration email on that page.

  • Failing to register within 30 days of the first notice brings administrative penalties starting at $25 a day for days 31 to 45 and rising to $100 a day from day 76.
  • Municipal court citations are listed at $180, $330 and $480 when paid within 10 days, and $200, $350 and $500 afterward.
  • Family members living rent-free in a house the owner does not occupy still trigger registration.

If you are selling a rented house, ask the city whether unpaid penalties are attached to the property, because the page says penalties must be paid before a property can be registered.

sections.h2: Do game-day and vacation rentals count as rentals in College Station?
sections.html: Yes. The city's definition of rental property names vacation rentals and game-day rentals, and it also covers houses where a family member lives but the owner does not. Buyers who plan to rent the house will ask whether it is registered, so collect the registration record before you list. Ask the city's code enforcement office whether a separate short-term rental permit applies to your address.

sections.h2: How do College Station property taxes work for a seller?
sections.html:
Brazos Central Appraisal District values every parcel, local governments set rates, and the tax assessor-collector sends bills. The district's process page lists January 1 as the valuation date, notices of appraised value from mid April to about June 1, and a protest deadline of May 15 or 30 days after the notice.

Statewide, the Comptroller says Texas has no state property tax, appraisals are tied to January 1 ownership, and the bill is due upon receipt in October with delinquency starting February 1 after a January 31 deadline. Unpaid tax carries a six percent penalty plus one percent interest in the first month, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

  • A tax lien attaches every January 1, and the owner on that date is liable even after a sale.
  • Exemption applications are generally due by April 30, and the district's contact page lists an email address for sending them.
  • Heirs not named on a recorded deed can still apply by sending an affidavit, the prior owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation.

sections.h2: What is the residence homestead exemption and how does it affect buyers?
sections.html:
The Comptroller says school districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, and any taxing unit may adopt a local option exemption of up to 20 percent of appraised value, no less than $5,000. A homeowner must live in the house as a principal residence and cannot claim another homestead.

A buyer who takes title after January 1 can get the exemption for the rest of that year at once if the prior owner never received it. That detail helps your buyer and may help you in negotiation if the house has no exemption on file. The same Comptroller page says residence homesteads have a 10 percent yearly appraisal cap once the exemption has been in place.

Owners aged 65 or older or disabled get an additional $60,000 school exemption and a school tax ceiling that can follow them to a new Texas home. Disabled veterans have exemptions that run from $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating up to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent, and a total exemption applies to a 100 percent disabled veteran's homestead.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled at closing in College Station?
sections.html:
The title company prorates them, so ask for the tax certificate and the proration figures before you sign. Because the lien attaches on January 1 and the owner on that date is liable, a sale in the fall usually involves your share of the current year, even if the bill has not arrived.

A seller who knows of a delinquency can ask the collector to waive penalty and interest, but the Comptroller says the tax generally must be paid within 21 days of learning of it and the waiver requested in writing within 181 days after the delinquency date. Some collectors allow delinquent installment plans up to 36 months on a residence homestead.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, in foreclosure or has tenants?
sections.html:
Each situation has its own clock. Texas law gives four years from death to probate a will, and the State Law Library says a muniment of title can pass the property when no administration is needed, with the order and will filed with the county clerk where the land sits.

For foreclosure, the State Law Library describes a notice of default, a 20-day window to reinstate, and a notice of sale given at least 21 days before an auction held on the first Tuesday of the month. A house with a tenant needs lawful notice: Texas generally requires at least three days written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, and eviction cases go to justice court.

  • Inherited house: confirm who holds title with a recorded deed or court order before listing.
  • Pre-foreclosure: pay off or sell before the first Tuesday sale date.
  • Tenant in place: cash buyers often buy subject to the lease or after the tenant leaves.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded after a sale in Brazos County?
sections.html:
The county clerk records deeds in the county where the property sits. The Texas Courts county clerk manual says a conveyance can be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer, or sworn before two witnesses.

The manual lists a recording fee of $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus records management, archive and technology fees. Ask the title company to confirm the current total with the clerk.

faqs.q: Can a College Station landlord sell a house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. The sale does not end a lease, so a buyer either takes the house with the tenant or waits until the lease ends. Any notice to vacate must follow Texas rules, and registered rental properties need their city registration in good standing.

faqs.q: Is rental registration still required if I sell my College Station house?
faqs.a: Registration applies while you own a non-owner-occupied house. The city page says to email rental registration staff when you no longer own a property so the record is removed, and unpaid penalties must be settled before a registration is completed.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax on a College Station home?
faqs.a: The county tax assessor-collector sends bills in October based on values set by Brazos Central Appraisal District. Contact the appraisal district for values, exemptions and protests, and the tax office for bills and payments.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the May 15 protest deadline in Brazos County?
faqs.a: The district lists May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later, as the protest deadline. If you miss it, ask the appraisal district about late filing options before the taxes become delinquent on February 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I owe back taxes on my College Station house?
faqs.a: Yes, the delinquent amount is paid from the proceeds at closing, and the title company will request a payoff. Penalty and interest keep growing each month, and attorney fees of up to 20 percent can apply after July 1 where the taxing unit has that contract.
